feature_results.rationale: Devin CLI documents user-configured command and prompt hooks at PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest and other lifecycle events. A command receives tool inputs and can deny an action with exit code 2 or a block decision, or rewrite arguments using updatedInput. This is an active lifecycle mechanism, not a passive session notification webhook. The positive finding is scoped to local Devin; it is not a claim about classic Cascade or universal cloud hook support.

evidence.excerpt: The script receives event data on stdin and can block the action by exiting with code `2`
The rewritten arguments are merged into the tool call before it runs — the agent executes the updated command instead of the original.

a `hooks.json` at the plugin root registers
  [lifecycle hooks](/cli/extensibility/hooks/lifecycle-hooks) in local Devin
  sessions (the CLI and Devin Desktop) where the plugin is installed.

constraints.description: Confirmed in Devin CLI; plugin hook registration is documented for local Devin sessions in CLI and Devin Desktop. Do not extrapolate this to classic Cascade or every cloud surface.

Plugin hooks are best effort and fail open when loading or execution fails. They are not reliable mandatory guardrails. Standalone command hooks block with exit 2; other nonzero exits log an error without blocking.
Command-hook exit codes other than 0 and 2 are errors that do not block the action.

feature_results.rationale: Devin Cloud security profiles provide configurable hostname and CIDR destination allowlists, blocking other outbound traffic from the session machine. Mandatory profiles constrain lower-level overrides. This is network-specific enforcement, not merely isolated compute. Devin CLI also documents configurable sandbox network filtering, but with distinct stability and platform limitations.

evidence.excerpt: A network policy is an allowlist of destinations the session's machine is permitted to reach. All other outbound connections are blocked.
The restriction applies to all network access from the session — shell commands, browsing, package installs, and scripts alike.
Configure domain-level network filtering for the sandbox in the [`sandbox` section of your config file](/cli/reference/configuration/config-file#sandbox) (user config only).

constraints.description: Required destinations such as Devin's git proxy are automatically allowed; MCP access is governed separately. Profile changes apply at boot/wake, not automatically to already-running sessions.
On Outposts, Devin publishes spec.network_policy but does not install firewall rules. The customer must enforce the policy on its own infrastructure.
Devin CLI sandboxing is unsupported on Windows; Linux requires bubblewrap and socat. Network filtering requires an active sandbox.
The CLI documentation explicitly warns that sandbox network filtering is currently unstable. This limitation is CLI-specific, not a statement about Cloud security profiles.
Enterprise-wide profiles and hard-floor enterprise defaults are enterprise-account controls; organization profiles are documented separately without a precise plan entitlement table.

access_gaps: Authoritative https://devin.ai/pricing returned HTTP 404; exact security-profile plan entitlements could not be checked there.

feature_results.rationale: Devin CLI documents /steps and /revert <step>: a single operation reverts file changes from the selected conversation step onward and rewinds the conversation. This covers multi-step session changes, rather than a single file or hunk. The finding is scoped to Devin CLI; command-history navigation and fresh Cloud environment snapshots are not treated as rollback.

evidence.excerpt: Revert file changes from a specific step onwards and rewind the conversation to before that step

constraints.description: Verified for Devin CLI interactive sessions. Equivalent rollback in the Devin Cloud web interface was not established.
The documented restoration covers file changes and conversation state; it does not promise reversal of external side effects, remote deployments, or arbitrary process state.

feature_results.rationale: Enterprise administrators have event-level audit logs via API, including login, session lifecycle, role, settings and security-profile actions, plus consumption reporting. Organization usage metrics are also documented. Partial follows the assigned criterion for logging limited to an enterprise tier; it does not mean the available enterprise logs are merely aggregate.

evidence.excerpt: Requires a [service user](/api-reference/v3/service-users/members-service-users) or [personal access token](/api-reference/personal-access-tokens) with the `ViewAccountAuditLogs` permission at the enterprise level.
**Audit logs** — every login is recorded, providing visibility into who has accessed Devin
Get aggregated usage metrics for the organization.

Enterprise admins can break consumption down by Organization from the [Consumption](https://app.devin.ai/settings/consumption) page in Enterprise Settings. Org admins can break it down by user from [Consumption Analytics](https://app.devin.ai/settings/analytics?tab=consumption) inside Organization Settings.

constraints.description: Enterprise audit-log access requires ViewAccountAuditLogs. Equivalent self-serve per-event audit access was not established.
Explicit audit-log API time ranges must be 100 days or less. Requests without time filters return available history subject to pagination.
Organization usage metrics require a service user or PAT with ViewOrgMetrics.

feature_results.rationale: Devin Review is a dedicated hosted PR review workflow with bug and security findings, actionable comments, and auto-review on PR creation or new commits. This is not merely a request to review code in ordinary chat. Provider capabilities and write authentication vary.

evidence.excerpt: Devin can automatically review PRs without you having to manually trigger it.

Leave comments, approve PRs, request changes—all within Devin Review, synced
    to GitHub.

constraints.description: GitHub write features require a GitHub App connection; PAT-based connections are read-only. Connected GitLab, Azure DevOps and Bitbucket Data Center also support auto-review with provider-specific capabilities.
Bitbucket Data Center requires version 8.16 or later; Bitbucket Cloud is not supported by Devin Review.
Teams AI review consumes shared on-demand credits; exhausting credits leaves the smart diff viewer rather than AI-powered review. Public GitHub PR reviews are free without an account.
Review execution is permission-gated. Draft PRs are skipped until marked ready.

queries: FETCH https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/devin-review.md (first 16000 characters, including provider matrix and Auto-Review)

feature_results.rationale: Devin Cloud documents instruction-driven structural refactors including extracting shared code into libraries and monorepo restructuring. Its refactoring prompts explicitly require preserving functionality, updating dependent code, imports and dependencies, and passing tests. This exceeds single-symbol renaming and is not an IDE-native manual refactor command. Behavior preservation is a requested and tested postcondition, not an unconditional correctness guarantee.

evidence.excerpt: 2. **Code migrations, refactors, and modernization**

* Monorepo to submodule conversions
   * Removing unused feature flags
   * Extracting common code into libraries

Requirements:
- Maintain all existing functionality
- Follow the conventions in `[example file]`
- Update any dependent code

constraints.description: Preserving behavior must be specified and verified with the repository's tests; the documentation recommends explicit completion criteria and well-scoped steps for complex work.

feature_results.rationale: Official documentation explicitly describes test generation following team playbooks and provides a targeted Add Test Coverage template for a file, module or function, asking for unit and integration tests. This documents deliberate test generation, not incidental code output. The npm example is a template, not a stated language restriction.

evidence.excerpt: Devin writes tests from human-provided [playbooks](/product-guides/creating-playbooks), following your team's testing patterns and conventions.
Add comprehensive test coverage for `[file/module/function]`.

2. Write unit tests for all public methods
3. Add integration tests if applicable

feature_results.rationale: Devin Cloud Agent mode explicitly supports end-to-end autonomous work involving code edits, commands, tests, debugging, and PR creation. Cognition's product page also states that Devin plans, writes, tests, and ships code on its own. This is open-ended task execution, not merely a fixed workflow or suggested edit.

evidence.excerpt: Agent mode is Devin's full autonomous mode where it can write code, run commands, browse the web, and complete complex tasks end-to-end.
Devin plans, writes, tests, and ships production code on its own

constraints.description: Use Agent mode for implementation; Ask mode is read-only exploration and planning. Clear success criteria and a configured development environment improve reliability.

Local CLI shell and write operations normally prompt; configurable permission modes reduce interruptions. Sandbox Autonomous mode still prompts for direct edit/write tools, and organization rules remain enforced.

feature_results.rationale: Cloud sessions continue working independently of the user's active terminal or laptop; the documented handoff workflow explicitly supports background migrations, batch jobs, and large refactors. Current release notes confirm asynchronous completion/attention notifications through the sidebar inbox and optional phone pushes.

evidence.excerpt: The cloud session gets its own VM with a shell, browser, and full repo access, so it can keep going after you close your laptop.
The bell in the sidebar collects notifications about your sessions, such as when Devin finishes working or needs your attention

constraints.description: The verified unattended workflow runs in Devin Cloud, including work handed off from the CLI. It is not a claim that a local process survives shutdown.
Execution is subject to plan usage quota, on-demand credits, and configured session spending limits.
Settings > Notifications controls which events appear in the inbox and which are also pushed to the user's phone.

feature_results.rationale: Ask Devin documents automatically indexed repositories, natural-language codebase questions and code-cited answers using advanced code search. The official Devin 2.0 announcement likewise describes agentic search and Deep Mode. Neither fetched page establishes meaning-based retrieval ranked by relevance rather than text matching, as the assigned has criterion requires. Natural-language Q&A plus indexing alone is insufficient to prove the underlying retrieval semantics. Search summaries described this as semantic search, but their stronger wording was not present on the original pages. No current-file-only limitation was established, so partial would also be misleading.

evidence.excerpt: Ask Devin uses advanced code search capabilities to produce detailed, accurate, and well-cited answers grounded in your codebase.
Devin Search enables you to ask questions directly about your codebase, and quickly get detailed answers with cited code.

constraints.description: The documented codebase Q&A workflow requires repository access and completed indexing; the default branch is indexed, with additional branches selectable.

feature_results.rationale: Devin CLI documents custom agent Markdown definitions with a system prompt, description, model override and independent allowed-tools restrictions. They become selectable worker profiles alongside built-in agents. However, the current guide explicitly marks custom subagents experimental, matching the assigned partial criterion even though prompt and tool scoping are documented. Custom profiles are local-only, not supported in cloud sessions; built-in cloud agent options, skills and playbooks are not substituted for user-authored subagents.

evidence.excerpt: Custom subagents are **experimental**. The format, behavior, and configuration options may change in future releases.
Custom subagents let you create specialized workers with their own system prompts, tool restrictions, and model overrides
**Subagents** (`agents/<name>.md` or `agents/<name>/AGENT.md`) load in local Devin agents only (CLI and Devin Desktop), not in cloud sessions.

constraints.description: Custom subagents are explicitly experimental; format, behavior and configuration may change.
Custom profiles load in local Devin CLI and Devin Desktop agents only, not cloud sessions.
A custom profile can pin model; otherwise it uses the default subagent model, not necessarily the parent's model. Organization model policy can constrain availability or disable subagents.
allowed-tools restricts tool scope but cannot grant ask_user_question, which is always withheld. Background subagents cannot request new permissions; unapproved calls are denied.

A negative finding cannot be completed: the product homepage returned 404, the separate Desktop/API documentation inventories were not exhaustively inspected, and the scripted-tool terminology remains insufficiently explained. feature_results.rationale: The Devin security page describes an actionable Data Controls training opt-out for paid plans, enabling Zero Data Retention with model providers after opting out. This is not enterprise-only: Pro, Max and Teams are paid self-serve plans. Enterprise data is not used for training without prior written consent. Scope resolves the apparent difference between general default training language and enterprise no-training language.

evidence.excerpt: If you're on a paid plan, you can opt out at any time on the Data Controls settings page. After you opt out, your data will not be used for training and Zero Data Retention will be enabled with our model providers. On the Teams plan, only an administrator can exercise the opt-out.
If you are an Enterprise customer, we will never train on your data without your express prior written consent.

constraints.description: The actionable opt-out is documented for paid plans, not Free. Teams requires an administrator to opt out. Enterprise has a separate prior-written-consent requirement for training.

Zero Data Retention is enabled with model providers, not a blanket promise that Cognition retains no session/customer data. Security documentation retains customer data during the relationship and feedback/interaction data as needed.
Platform terms state ZDR does not preclude safety/abuse review retention or legally compelled retention/disclosure.

feature_results.rationale: Security Swarm documents agentic source-code vulnerability analysis and importing scanner reports. Its GitHub Advisory Database reference is an evaluation benchmark, not proof of operational dependency-to-CVE matching. Devin Desktop documentation recommends Snyk and Checkmarx extensions for open-source dependencies but does not document the required vulnerability database integration or its findings feeding the Devin assistant. Generic MCP support, arbitrary audit commands and dependency upgrades do not establish SCA. Material product-page access gaps preclude not_found.

Easily find and fix issues in your code, open source dependencies, infrastructure as code configurations with fast and accurate scans

feature_results.rationale: Devin Desktop explicitly documents per-hunk diff zones with accept/reject controls and Command-generated diffs with accept/reject actions. However, the fetched official text does not establish that proposed edits remain unwritten to disk until acceptance, as the assigned has criterion specifically requires. Devin Cloud's live IDE diff and PR review are not evidence of pre-write review. Devin Review also supports reviewing suggested chat edits before committing them to a PR branch, but pre-commit approval is not the same as pre-disk-write approval. Neither has nor the whole-file-only partial criterion is established under this strict definition.

evidence.excerpt: When an agent edits files, Devin Desktop displays **diff zones** — inline highlighted regions in the editor that show exactly what changed, with accept and reject controls for each hunk. All agents use diff zones by default.

You can accept, reject, or follow-up a generation by clicking the corresponding code lens above the generated diff, or by using the appropriate shortcuts (`Cmd/Ctrl+Enter` to accept, `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Backspace` to reject).

Ask the chat agent to make code edits. Review the suggested changes, then
    apply them as a commit to the PR branch without leaving Devin Review.

constraints.description: Per-hunk accept/reject controls are documented in Devin Desktop, not established as a pre-write gate for autonomous Devin Cloud sessions.
Agent diff zones can be disabled for non-Cascade agents; in that configuration edits are applied directly and the toolbar has a dismiss button rather than accept/reject controls.

Devin Review chat edits support GitHub and GitLab; GitHub write features require a GitHub App connection. Azure DevOps cannot apply chat edits, and Bitbucket Data Center commits chat edits one file at a time.

feature_results.rationale: Devin's general security documentation explicitly states both in-transit and at-rest encryption. The Devin-specific enterprise architecture page confirms both for customer data in Cloud and Customer Dedicated deployments. No encryption algorithm or protection of customer-operated Outpost disks is inferred from the general statement.

evidence.excerpt: All data transmission is encrypted in transit and at rest.
Customer data stays encrypted in transit and at rest, and is processed in an isolated tenant.

constraints.description: Outposts shift infrastructure security and operation to the customer. These vendor-hosted encryption statements should not be treated as proof of customer-managed machine/disk encryption.

feature_results.rationale: Devin Enterprise documents SAML 2.0 and OIDC identity-provider connections alongside configurable organization- and account-level roles and fine-grained permissions. Roles can be assigned to individual users and IdP groups. This meets both SSO and RBAC criteria, not merely team membership.

Enterprise administrators can create custom roles with specific permissions and assign them to users or IdP groups, providing granular control over what actions users can perform within your Devin Enterprise deployment.

constraints.description: SSO onboarding and custom granular RBAC are documented for Devin Enterprise.

An external SAML/OIDC-compliant IdP is required. Cognition configures the connection; default email/GitHub/Google login remains enabled unless the Disable default login connections option is selected.
Each user can currently have only one role per organization and one account-level role.

feature_results.rationale: No current zero-network operating mode was established for Devin Cloud. Enterprise deployment documentation says the brain remains in Cognition's cloud, and Outposts explicitly retains cloud inference even on customer machines. Separately, the federal FAQ says fully air-gapped Devin CLI/Desktop versions are being finalized, while the CLI reference already mentions air-gapped builds and model endpoint connectivity. These are scope differences, not evidence that the whole Devin product currently works without any network. Air-gapped operation can still require an internal network to model endpoints; no available page establishes zero connectivity, availability, or the full core-functionality coverage of that special build. Therefore neither has nor partial is substantiated, and a complete negative finding would be inappropriate.

evidence.excerpt: Devin's agent loop (inference and planning) continues to run in Devin's cloud, while all command execution, file edits, and repository access happen on machines you operate.
We are finalizing versions of Devin Desktop and Devin CLI that can be run fully air-gapped and on-prem.
`devin airgap doctor` is only present in air-gapped builds of the CLI.

constraints.description: Customer-hosted Outposts still requires an outbound HTTPS connection to Devin Cloud; self-hosted command execution is not offline inference.
The federal FAQ describes fully air-gapped CLI/Desktop versions as being finalized rather than documenting general availability.
The airgap diagnostic exists only in special air-gapped CLI builds; it checks licensing and configured model endpoint connectivity, without documenting a zero-network configuration.

feature_results.rationale: Devin's GitHub integration explicitly documents pushing branches as a regular contributor, and a /devin PR command starts a session that can fix a check and push a commit. These are executed repository operations, not plain-text suggestions for the user to run.

evidence.excerpt: These permissions enable Devin to work in your repositories as a regular contributor—pushing branches, opening pull requests, and participating in PR discussions.

constraints.description: The documented GitHub workflow requires the Devin GitHub connection and access to the relevant repository.

feature_results.rationale: Devin CLI documents non-interactive --print execution, ATIF conversation export, bypass permission mode, and skipping workspace trust checks for scripts/CI. Cloud Devin also has an explicit --cloud -p mode, but it prints a response and exits while the cloud session persists; that is not a documented completion-based CI success signal. The checked reference documents non-zero status for doctor diagnostics, not coding-task exit-code semantics. Accordingly the unattended CLI surface is real, but the full structured-output-and-meaningful-task-exit-code criterion is not established. Hook or diagnostic exit codes and AI-search assertions about standard CLI conventions were not treated as task-execution evidence.

evidence.excerpt: | `--print [PROMPT]` | `-p` | | Print response and exit (non-interactive mode). Optionally accepts an inline prompt. |
| `--export [PATH]` | | | Export conversation to a file after each turn (ATIF format). Uses a default path if none is provided. |
`--cloud -p` starts a session, sends one prompt, prints Devin's response to stdout, and exits. The session persists; resume it with `devin --cloud -r`.

constraints.description: Non-interactive print mode fails in an untrusted workspace unless trust is already established or --respect-workspace-trust false is supplied.
Default and accept-edits modes can require action approvals. Bypass auto-approves tool calls but does not override admin-enforced deny or ask rules.
Cloud print mode exits after a response, not necessarily after the persistent cloud coding session completes.
Cloud CLI usage requires an authenticated Devin account.

feature_results.rationale: Current Devin Desktop Tab documentation describes AI-powered inline suggestions based on coding context, disappearing when typing continues without acceptance, and a traditional Autocomplete mode at the cursor. Tab accepts and Esc cancels suggestions; no chat prompt is required. Scope is Devin Desktop's editor. The official FAQ explicitly identifies the Windsurf-to-Devin Desktop rebrand, so this finding is not an attribution of unrelated Windsurf plugin functionality to Devin Cloud. The Cloud session IDE also lists Tab autocomplete, but the detailed confirmation here rests on current Desktop documentation.

evidence.excerpt: Devin Desktop Tab provides AI-powered code suggestions with Tab to Jump, Tab to Import, and inline suggestions, powered by our custom model.
Suggestions will also disappear if you continue typing or navigating without accepting them.
**Autocomplete** is a more traditional autocomplete mode that appears at your cursor.
Devin Desktop is the new name for Windsurf. It's the same IDE, same editor, and has the same features, but **unified under the Devin brand**.

constraints.description: Detailed inline-completion confirmation is for Devin Desktop. It does not establish equivalent as-you-type completion in every Devin CLI ACP editor integration or legacy Windsurf plugin.
Tab is powered by a custom in-house model; this is separate from choosing a conversational coding-agent model.
Completion mode can be set to Supercomplete, Autocomplete, or Off. The page does not enumerate language coverage.
The Desktop FAQ states that Teams users need a full seat for Devin Desktop. Desktop access should not be assumed from a Cloud-only enterprise SKU.

feature_results.rationale: Devin Enterprise offers support-enabled public-code attribution filtering for cloud file-editing tools and Devin CLI. Partial follows the assigned criteria because this is enterprise-only, with no self-serve toggle, and generated-output IP indemnification was not established. The public MSA's service indemnity excludes Customer Data, whose definition includes Outputs; it is not evidence of indemnifying generated code. Ownership of output alone is also insufficient.

evidence.excerpt: When a match against public code is detected, the write is blocked and Devin rewrites the implementation instead.

Attribution filtering is available on **Enterprise plans** and is not enabled by default. There is currently no self-serve toggle — to enable it for your organization, reach out to [support@cognition.ai](mailto:support@cognition.ai) or contact your Cognition account team.

When attribution filtering is enabled for your team, code generated by Devin CLI is checked against a corpus of publicly available code: file edits that match public code are automatically reverted, and matching code blocks in chat responses are flagged while the agent is instructed to rewrite them.
(vii) Customer Data.

constraints.description: Enterprise only, off by default, enabled through support/account team rather than a self-serve toggle.
